key_insight: Rotational equivariance is a useful inductive bias for learned subgrid-scale closures, especially when combined with nonlocal receptive fields.
engineering_relevance: For LES turbulence modeling, equivariant nonlocal closures can improve accuracy and generalization while using fewer parameters and less training data.
method: Compared data-augmented non-equivariant models against rotationally equivariant models.
Tested both pointwise and nonlocal architectures for subgrid-scale closure.
Evaluated matched-parameter models on spatiotemporal, anisotropy, and Reynolds-number generalization in turbulent channel flow.
evidence_signal: The equivariant nonlocal model achieved the highest correlation on every generalization test at about half the parameter count of its non-equivariant counterpart, while pointwise models did not outperform the Clark baseline.
watch_item: Benefits depend on receptive field and data regime, so gains may be smaller for local architectures or settings with limited isotropy in the training data.
paper_title: Rotational equivariance and locality in data-driven subgrid-scale closures
